messages:
ops-bot: [ALERT] hosted-usw2-gpu-pool-4: p95_queue_time spiked from 1.8s -> 7.2s, headroom_pct dropped to 0.8%, admission_control=ENABLED. link: https://dash.redwood/hosted/usw2/pool-4?panel=queue

alex: saw this, looks like a sustained spike for ~4m. Dashboard shows repeated 100% occupancy bursts around 14:02-14:06 UTC. Anyone oncall? :eyes:

monica: pinging oncall. I also see an odd step in the metrics stream — bandwidth for metrics-collector v2 jumped and we have a lot of prefix cache misses that line up with the spike. Not sure if it's real or telemetry noise.

kai: quick PromQL to check admission rejects by reason:
```
sum(rate(admission_rejected_total{pool="usw2-pool-4"}[1m])) by (reason)
```
run that and filter reason=\"capacity\" vs reason=\"rate_limit\".

alex: ran it — majority are reason=capacity (slot exhaustion), small minority rate_limit. Looks like real saturation, not just the alert feed. Also correlates with a surge of long-seq requests from a few hosts (seq_len > 4096).

monica: ok that matches the KV-cache missstorm theory. Large contexts result in lower batching efficiency and bigger KV churn. Dashboard panel shows svc_kv_cache_miss_rate spiking 4x at same times.

alex: mitigation proposal: temporarily cap hosted free-tier max_context to 2048 for us-west-2 and enable spillover routing to dedicated-usw2-temp. Rollout plan: feature flag -> soft throttle -> full cap if spike persists. Thoughts?

sarah: product concern: any customer-visible regressions? We should prefer spillover over hard caps where possible. What are the cost implications of spillover to dedicated?

mike: rough calc — if we spill 15% of requests to dedicated for 6 hours, unit cost up by ~12% for that period. But outage risk and p95 tail reduction likely worth it. If we do a hard cap, some requests will fail or degrade quality which is worse for SLAs.

kai: ops commands I can run now to start soft spillover:
```
# enable spillover routing to dedicated pool
redwoodctl routing update --pool hosted-usw2-pool-4 --spillover dedicated-usw2-temp --threshold 0.92
```
I'll schedule a 5m canary then open to all.

monica: also recommend tuning the alert: current p95_queue_time alert is a 1m eval and is noisy. Change to a 5m sliding window with a 3m sustained threshold before firing, and ignore samples where headroom_pct < 0 (bad telemetry). I'll open a PR to alerts repo.

alex: PR to reduce free-tier max_context flag created and staged: feature/gated/usw2-cap-2048. I'll keep it soft (429 with retry-after header for non-critical routes).

ops-bot: oncall-bot: create incident?

oncall-bot: Incident INCIDENT-20240402-71 created for "usw2 pool-4 saturation". Assigned to @monica & @alex. Spillover routing enabled (canary). Link: https://incidents.redwood/IN-71

monica: follow-ups: 1) add a dashboard panel bucketed by seq_len (<=512, 513-2048, 2049-4096, >4096) to see which buckets drive admission. 2) add smoothing to headroom_pct ingestion (5m EWMA) so transient spikes don't flip alerts. 3) run a retrospective on the origin of long-context surge (client IDs show a couple of suspicious hosts).

alex: I've kicked off node refill request (+2 gpus) to capacity-ops for a soft scale. ETA ~ 40m. If refill misses, we'll keep spillover on and keep the cap.

sarah: please log estimated cost impact & customer list touched in the incident doc. I'll notify support for high-value customers.

mike: noted — will compute cost delta and post in the incident doc in 10m.

monica: closing notes for now — canary spillover looks stable, p95 down to ~2.1s after canary. Leaving alert suppression for 10m and will follow up with PRs for alert tuning and dashboard. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
